_comment: CASE 2B -- PARTIAL PARTICIPATION, LP (multipath) leg. mini_2gpu_1nic (4 hosts x 2 GPUs = 8 GPUs, ONE shared 100Gbps NIC per host off the PCIe root complex, 2 leaf + 2 spine, 16 fine nodes) with 4 of the 8 GPUs active: [0, 2, 3, 5]. The placement is deliberately LOPSIDED -- 3 participants behind leaf0 and 1 behind leaf1, and one host contributing BOTH of its GPUs -- which is what makes the shared NIC, not the fabric, the thing that binds. Read against mini_2gpu_1nic_alltoall.json (all 8 active, where the leaf cut binds) and against its MILP partner.
_known_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION, ACCEPTED -- MILP timing on a non-uniform-bandwidth topology at a sub-chunk epoch. This topology mixes 100Gbps host ports with 50Gbps leaf-spine uplinks, and this file's pinned 0.08 s epoch is SHORTER than one chunk on the 50Gbps link (6.25 GB/s x 0.08 s = 0.5 GB against a 1 GB chunk), so get_beta_num_back returns beta = 1 there. In that regime the MILP's cut-through accounting under-charges TIME: allgather.py pays the store-and-forward cost (1 epoch + beta) ONCE at the first GPU->switch hop and charges every later fabric hop only propagation delay (see the branches at allgather.py switch->switch and the switch->GPU buffer credit), so the delivery epoch it credits is 1 + beta(FIRST hop) instead of the correct 1 + max(beta over the legs used) = ceil(chunk / min bandwidth along the path). CONSEQUENCE: in a MILP schedule from this file, 3-Epochs_Required, 4-Collective_Finish_Time and 5-Algo_Bandwidth are OPTIMISTIC and must not be quoted -- the ROUTING (7-Flows and 8-Chunk paths) is what the file is for, and real timing comes from simulating that routing. Measured on case 1A at this epoch: the MILP reports 0.08 s while every 50Gbps leg on its own chosen path needs 0.16 s to clock the chunk out; the identical run with switch_pipeline false (which does charge the -1 and beta) reports 0.48 s. The LP is NOT affected: continuous flow can be split across epochs, so it has no beta machinery and its per-epoch row (capacity x epoch_duration) is exact -- which is why the fine epoch is kept here rather than coarsened, since it is what makes the LP's makespan exact instead of rounded up. mini_2gpu_2nic (case 3A) is structurally immune: its links are uniform 100Gbps, so one chunk always fits one epoch and beta is 0 everywhere.
_participation: active GPUs [0, 2, 3, 5]; passive GPUs [1, 4, 6, 7]. Node map (class-major, declaration order): 0/1 = srv0.gpu0/gpu1, 2/3 = srv1, 4/5 = srv2, 6/7 = srv3; 8-11 = srv0-3.rc; 12/13 = leaf0/leaf1; 14/15 = spine0/spine1. srv0 and srv1 hang off leaf0, srv2 and srv3 off leaf1. So the active set is: srv0 contributing gpu0 alone, srv1 contributing BOTH gpus, srv2 contributing gpu1 alone, and srv3 contributing NOTHING -- srv3 is a fully passive host, present as a relay only. Passive GPUs still forward (teccl/solvers/demand.py::_demand_sources only removes them from the demand tensor), and num_chunks 1 still means one chunk per (src, dst) PAIR: the chunk axis is widened by the ACTIVE count, so this is 4 x 3 = 12 chunks of 1 GB, not 56.
_expected: T* = 0.32 s = 4 epochs, set by srv1's SHARED NIC and by nothing else. srv1 has both of its GPUs active, and each sends to gpu0 and to gpu5; the gpu2<->gpu3 pair rides the 56 GBps intra-host NVLink bridge and never touches the NIC, so the NIC carries 2 x 2 = 4 GB = 0.32 s at 12.5 GB/s (ingress mirrors it: 2 chunks from gpu0 + 2 from gpu5). The 0.08 s epoch divides that exactly, so the LP's makespan is its true bound with nothing lost to the grid. Everything else is slacker: the leaf cut is 3 GB per direction ({0,2,3} x {5}) against 12.5 GB/s = 0.24 s; srv0's and srv2's NICs carry 3 GB = 0.24 s; the 200Gbps PCIe leg carries at most 2 chunks per GPU = 0.16 s. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE CASE: with all 8 GPUs active the cut binds at 1.28 s and the shared NIC is slack at 0.96 s; dropping half the GPUs but leaving one host FULLY active inverts that, so the cost of the shared NIC is paid by whichever host has both of its GPUs in the collective. THE MULTIPATH CHECK: one 50Gbps uplink carries 0.5 GB per epoch, so 2 GB over 4 epochs -- less than the 3 GB the cut must pass -- and BOTH spines must carry cross-leaf flow in any optimal solution. Inspect that the LP splits per-PAIR (a single 1 GB demand fanned 0.5/0.5, which the MILP cannot do) and not merely per-aggregate. THE RELAY CHECK: relaying through a passive GPU relieves neither srv1's NIC (gpu2's peer gpu3 is itself active, behind the same NIC) nor the leaf cut, so objective_type 6's relay tier should keep every path direct; a detour through srv3 is a red flag.
_epoch_note: epoch_type 3 (USER_INPUT) with epoch_duration PINNED to 0.08 s = 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, one 100Gbps host port. Deliberately NOT the SLOWEST_LINK value (0.16 s, the 50Gbps uplink) that the full-participation files on this topology use: at 0.16 s the LP's answer is rounded up to the epoch grid, and pinning 0.08 s is what makes the LP's makespan land exactly on its true bound. The price is paid by the MILP leg only, and it is a KNOWN, ACCEPTED inaccuracy in its reported time -- see _known_limitation. Both legs share this clock so the routing comparison stays controlled.
_symmetry_note: symmetry true is SAFE under partial participation. Orbit averaging verifies every candidate permutation against the DEMAND matrix as well as the capacity matrix (symmetrize.py::preserves_demand), so any automorphism mapping an active GPU onto a passive one is rejected: srv0's gpu0<->gpu1, srv2's gpu4<->gpu5 and the leaf swap (leaf0 carries 3 participants, leaf1 carries 1) all go. What survives is srv1's gpu2<->gpu3 swap and the spine swap -- exactly the two orbits worth balancing here.
_why_flat_only: hierarchical is false and CANNOT be true on this topology, independently of participation: the host's one external link is the NIC, owned by `rc` rather than by a GPU, and DslTopology._build_cell requires a cell's external links to be owned by its GPUs. The .topo file therefore does not mark these hosts as cells.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. The path is relative to the repo root.
